newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia industrial output down 3.5 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Colombia industrial output down 3.5 pct in 1996.

text.p: Colombia's industrial output, excluding coffee processing, fell 3.5 percent in 1996 compared to a 3.9 percent rise in 1995, according to figures released by the government's National Statistics Department.
The fall took Colombia's industrial output to its lowest level in 12 years and was due to the sharp economic slowdown seen in 1996, the statistics department said.

Taking into account coffee processing industrial output was down 2.94 percent. The biggest falls were seen in the transportation equipment, chemicals, beverages and paper products sector, the National Statistics Department report said. The biggest growth were seen in refined oil products, foods and textiles.

Industrial sales fell 1.46 percent, according to the report. Industrial wages, meanwhile, increased an average 2.34 percent with white collar workers'salaries rising an average 3.29 percent and blue collar wages rising 1.53 percent on average, according to the statistics department.
